statement: A high-pass filter is an electronic filter and linear time-invariant system that passes signals with a frequency higher than a cutoff frequency $f_c$ and attenuates signals with frequencies lower than the cutoff frequency, characterized in a continuous-time first-order passive RC realization by the transfer function $\frac{V_{\text{out}}(s)}{V_{\text{in}}(s)} = \frac{sRC}{1 + sRC}$.

symbols.meaning: input voltage in the Laplace domain
output voltage in the Laplace domain
input resistor in first-order active filter
feedback resistor in first-order active filter
sampling interval between evenly spaced discrete-time samples
discrete input sample at index i
discrete output sample at index i

properties.property: The cutoff frequency for a first-order passive RC filter is $f_c = \frac{1}{2\pi \tau} = \frac{1}{2\pi RC}$, where $\tau = RC$ is the time constant.
properties.why: time constant $\tau = RC$ is inversely proportional to the cutoff frequency $f_c$

properties.property: At the cutoff frequency $f_c$, the filter's frequency response reaches $-3\text{ dB}$ referenced to the gain at infinite frequency.
properties.why: standard cutoff definition marking the half-power threshold relative to high-frequency passband gain

properties.property: A first-order active op-amp high-pass filter has transfer function $\frac{V_{\text{out}}(s)}{V_{\text{in}}(s)} = \frac{-s R_2 C}{1 + s R_1 C}$, with cutoff frequency $f_c = \frac{1}{2\pi R_1 C}$ and passband gain $-R_2/R_1$.
properties.why: active operational amplifier inverts and scales high frequencies by $-R_2/R_1$

properties.property: First-order high-pass filters perform differentiation for signals whose frequency band is well below the cutoff frequency.
properties.why: the linear time-invariant transfer function is proportional to $s$ for frequencies well below cutoff

properties.property: An $n$-th order high-pass filter has a stopband attenuation slope equal to $20n\text{ dB}$ per decade.
properties.why: cascading $n$ first-order high-pass stages compounds the roll-off slope

properties.property: The continuous-time RC filter discretizes to recurrence relation $y_i = \alpha y_{i-1} + \alpha (x_i - x_{i-1})$ with $\alpha = \frac{RC}{RC + \Delta_T}$ and cutoff $f_c = \frac{1-\alpha}{2\pi \alpha \Delta_T}$.
properties.why: Kirchhoff's laws and capacitor constitutive relations yield $V_{\text{out}}(t) = RC\left(\frac{dV_{\text{in}}}{dt} - \frac{dV_{\text{out}}}{dt}\right)$, which is discretized using differences over interval $\Delta_T$

assumptions.assumption: The filter operates as a linear time-invariant (LTI) system.
assumptions.breaks_when: Circuit components operate in nonlinear regimes (such as amplifier output clipping/saturation) or component parameters drift over time.

assumptions.assumption: In cascading passive filter stages, inter-stage loading is negligible or impedance matching is accounted for.
assumptions.breaks_when: Chained passive stages draw current and load prior stages without buffering or impedance matching.

assumptions.assumption: For discrete-time implementation, input samples are taken at uniformly spaced time intervals $\Delta_T$.
assumptions.breaks_when: Sampling periods vary due to clock jitter or non-uniform sampling.

failure_modes.signature: Waveform distortion and loss of linear frequency response
failure_modes.cause: Input signal amplitude amplified by the active passband gain $-R_2/R_1$ exceeds the operational amplifier supply rails.

failure_modes.signature: Deviation of attenuation slope and cutoff frequency from the expected $20n\text{ dB}$ per decade curve
failure_modes.cause: Cascading passive first-order stages without active buffering or proper impedance matching.

failure_modes.signature: Output reflects the time derivative of the signal rather than preserving signal shape
failure_modes.cause: Input signal frequency spectrum lies well below the filter cutoff frequency $f_c$.

failure_modes.signature: Excessive response delay and oversensitivity to small inputs (large $\alpha$) or overly fast decay with broad stopband attenuation (small $\alpha$)
failure_modes.cause: Parameter $\alpha$ is chosen inappropriately for the sampling interval $\Delta_T$ relative to the desired cutoff frequency $f_c$.
